main_question: Identify the structure. Name 2 structures that pass through its posterior
main_answer: Skull; structures passing through posterior openings (e.g., jugular foramen, hypoglossal canal) include the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), vagus nerve (CN X), accessory nerve (CN XI), and internal jugular vein.
main_explanation: The specimen is a lateral view of a human skull. The question asks to identify the general structure and name contents of a posterior foramen, likely the jugular foramen given the context of 'posterior' and common exam questions.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following structures passes through the hypoglossal canal?
supporting_question.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) passes through the hypoglossal canal to innervate the tongue muscles.
